headline: ICE's new officers are leaving far faster than Border Patrol's
description: People hired since September 2025 with no prior federal civilian or military service: running total each month, by whether they are still there.
notes: New to federal service: under 3 months of creditable federal civilian or military service at hire. ICE officers: series 1801 and 1811; Border Patrol agents: series 1896; both on the GL law-enforcement pay plan. OPM's public files don't follow individual people, so a departure's hire month is its effective month minus its years of service; in every month the running count who have left is at most the running count hired (checked). Transfers to other agencies are not counted. Recent months fill in as late records arrive. OPM's "other separation" category includes removals for discipline or performance, and deaths. Source: OPM Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) data, files through August 2026 (entry law-enforcement pay plan). Permanent appointments.

headline: How five occupations lost staff in 2025
description: Permanent staff who left in 2025, as a share of January 2025 staff, by how they left.
notes: Layoff (RIF): separations agencies coded as a reduction in force. Other: terminations (expired appointments and other) and OPM's "other separation", which includes removals for discipline or performance, and deaths. Retirement includes disability retirement. Transfers to other agencies are not counted. Source: OPM Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) data, files through August 2026. Permanent appointments.

description: Permanent federal employees who left each year, by years of service.
notes: *2026 is January through August only, so its bar is not comparable in height with the full years. DRP exits are included; transfers to other agencies are not. Source: OPM Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) data, files through August 2026. Permanent appointments.

headline: Long-serving staff are quitting at about their 2022 peak; retirements are lower
description: Permanent employees who left per month, per 1,000 on staff in January.
notes: January through August of every year. Each row is shaded against its own range. DRP exits are included, as quits or retirements depending on how OPM coded them. Transfers to other agencies are not counted. Retirement includes disability retirement. Records for recent months are still arriving: once they do, 2026* figures are likely 1-17% higher. Source: OPM Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) data, files through August 2026. Permanent appointments.

headline: Attorneys are quitting at nearly twice their old high
description: Permanent employees who quit per month, per 1,000 on staff in January.
notes: January through August of every year. Each row is shaded against its own range. Quits include DRP exits that OPM coded as quits. Attorneys: occupational series 0905 (general attorney); the agencies shown are those with 300+ attorneys whose attorneys are quitting at 2+ times their 2015-2024 high. Air traffic controllers: series 2152, every agency. Graduate degree: master's, professional or doctorate. Records for recent months are still arriving: once they do, 2026* quits are likely 1-9% higher. Source: OPM Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) data, files through August 2026. Permanent appointments.

headline: Pathways hiring is down about two-thirds
description: New hires through Pathways (internships, Recent Graduates, Presidential Management Fellows), January-August of each year, all appointment types.
notes: Pathways: OPM's pathways_group field on the hire record. *2026 is January through August; every year here covers the same months. Source: OPM Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) data, files through August 2026. All appointment types.

headline: Political appointees have refilled faster than in either of the last two terms
description: Political appointees, all appointment types: each January to November 2024, then monthly.
notes: Before November 2024 only January counts are read, so the lines skip the months between. Noncareer SES and limited-term SES are combined. Source: OPM Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) data, files through August 2026. All appointment types.

headline: At the Office of Management and Budget, Schedule Policy/Career is most of the agency
description: Staff in Schedule Policy/Career, August 2026: the 10 agencies with the most.
notes: It first appears in the June 2026 files. 10 of the 4,541 were hired into it; the files don't record moves between appointments, so the rest are counted as moved. Share of staff is of all the agency's staff, every appointment type. 4,476 hold it as a permanent appointment, so they are in every permanent figure in the post; 65 hold it as a nonpermanent one. Source: OPM Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI) data, files through August 2026. All appointment types.
